# The Mission Manifest

A Mission Manifest is one YAML document: the mission's goals, its `environment` and its `program`. Start from a template (topic `templates`). Read every field with `missionctl describe manifest` and one mapping with `missionctl describe manifest:SECTION`.

## How the keys refer to each other

- A `key` is a slug you choose: on the mission, each goal, objective, criterion and node. Node keys are unique in the mission.
- A node's `objectives` name goal or objective keys. Every goal needs a stage that names it, or whose output its criterion cites.
- A criterion's `evidence` is a list of output names that nodes declare under `outputs`.
- `acceptance` is a typed expression, never free text.
- `action_space` aliases name a capability's, agent's or plugin's `as`, or a node key.
- `depends_on` names sibling stages. An input's `from` and a gate's `packet` name `<node key>.<output name>`.
- A node's `environment` may only narrow the budget, governors and side effects it inherits.

`manifest` is `mission/v2`; `mission.application` is `APPLICATION_ID`.

| Where | Required |
| --- | --- |
| the document | `manifest` |
| `mission` | `key`, `title`, `application`, `goals`, `environment`, `program` |
| `brief` | `purpose`, `request` |
| `goals[]` | `key`, `description`, `criteria` |
| `goals[].objectives[]` | `key`, `description` |
| `goals[].criteria[]` | `key`, `description`, `evidence`, `acceptance` |
| `behavior: stage_graph` | `key`, `objectives`, `nodes` |
| `behavior: goal_loop` | `key`, `objective`, `action_space` |
| `behavior: agent_executor` | `key`, `objectives`, `instruction` |
| `behavior: human_gate` | `key`, `task` |
| a gate's `task` | `kind`, `prompt`, `reviewers` |
| `inputs[]` | `name` |
| `outputs[]` | `name` |

- `brief.purpose`: `research`, `content`, `system`, `other`
- `goals[].importance`: `primary`, `secondary`, `optional` (default `primary`)
- `task.kind`: `APPROVAL`, `QUESTION`, `SELECTION`, `REVIEW`, `POLICY_OVERRIDE`
- `outputs[].form`: `text`, `structured`, `file`, `collection`, `reference`, `code_change`, `effect_receipt`, `control_record` (default `structured`)
- `outputs[].enforcement`: `required`, `expected`, `optional` (default `required`)
- `inputs[].expand`: `inline`, `reference`, `materialize`, `auto` (default `auto`)
- `environment.side_effects[]`: `read_only`, `workspace_write`, `external_write_reversible`, `external_write_irreversible`, `spend`
- a capability entry's `kind`: `mcp_server`, `mcp_tool`, `skill_bundle`, `hook_script`, `subagent_profile`, `plugin`, `deterministic_executor`, `assessment`, `model_profile`, `sandbox_profile`, `context_bundle`, `tool`
- `outputs[].schema`: required for the forms `structured`, `control_record`, refused for `text`
- `acceptance`: exactly one of `assessment`, `human`, `schema`, `all`, `any`

The mission `environment` must hold, per lane:

| Lane | Required in `mission.environment` |
| --- | --- |
| `claude_agent_sdk`, `claude_cloud`, `codex`, `codex_cloud`, `cursor_local` | `model.profile`, `budget`, `governors`, `execution_environment`, `workspace.repo` |
| `claude_managed`, `codex_agents`, `cursor_cloud` | `model.profile`, `budget`, `governors`, `execution_environment` |
| `deep_agents` | `model.profile`, `budget`, `governors`, `sandbox` |

Your installation's bound sandbox profiles: `missionctl search --facet sandbox_profile`.

## Which acceptance can start

| `acceptance` on a goal owned by | a `goal_loop` program root | an `agent_executor` stage | a `human_gate` stage, `task.kind: APPROVAL`, `QUESTION`, `SELECTION`, `POLICY_OVERRIDE` | a `human_gate` stage, `task.kind: REVIEW` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `human: review_accept` | starts | refused | refused | starts |
| `human: approved` | refused | refused | starts | refused |
| `schema: <schema>@<revision>` | starts | starts | refused | refused |
| `assessment`, `all`, `any` | refused | refused | refused | refused |

A goal is owned by the last stage whose `objectives` name it or one of its objectives. `schema` starts only where every `evidence` output is a structured output of the owning node with that schema, and the schema is a published `artifact_schema`. A refused operator still compiles: the report says `ok: true` and `startable: false` and names it in `start_blockers` (`completion_evaluator_unavailable`). To accept text by review, end a Stage Graph with a `human_gate` whose `objectives` name every goal.

## When a promised output can be delivered

A `deep_agents` node submits the outputs it declares by calling `submit_output` (a text output has no other route), so name it in the node's `capabilities`: `{pin: tool.knowledge-submit-output@latest, kind: tool, as: submit_output}`. Every installation serves this tool: output promises are Mission Control's own records, with or without a knowledge binding. The other knowledge tools (`knowledge_read`, `knowledge_apply`, `report_register`, `report_derive`, `verify_claims`, `knowledge_read_intent`) are served only where the installation has a knowledge binding; elsewhere a node that names one does not start, and `missionctl preflight` names the missing binding. A text output is submitted as one inline text item and read back with `missionctl outputs content`; without `submit_output` the node's final message is transcript evidence only, the text promise stays unmet, and compile warns `output_submission_missing`.

On a lane that requires `sandbox`, a node starts only when `sandbox.profile` names a bound sandbox profile. The list above says what each one suits; read one in full (backend, command execution, network, files, lifetime) with `missionctl describe sandbox:PROFILE` and list them with `missionctl search --facet sandbox_profile`.
